description:
## Symptom (four lines of fz, all three backends)

    fn main() do
      acc = List.reverse([1, 2, 3], [])
      dbg(acc)                      # [3, 2, 1]   correct
      dbg(List.reverse(acc, []))    # []          WRONG -- Elixir: [1, 2, 3]
    end

`fz2 interp`, `fz2 run` (JIT) and `fz2 build` (AOT) all print `[3, 2, 1]` then
`[]`. Elixir's oracle (`Enum.reverse/2`, the same accumulate-onto-tail
contract) prints `[3, 2, 1]` then `[1, 2, 3]`. The second call returns the
INITIAL accumulator it was handed, i.e. its recursion result never reaches the
base clause's `tail` return.

Drop the intermediate `dbg(acc)` and the same program becomes a hard failure
instead of a silent one:

    fn main() do
      dbg(List.reverse(List.reverse([1, 2, 3], []), []))
    end
    => fz2 interp: backend value 1 is unbound

Same for `acc = List.reverse(xs, []); dbg(List.reverse(acc, []))` without the
`dbg(acc)` in between. The `dbg` is not incidental: it forces `acc` to
materialize, which converts the unbound-value crash into a wrong answer.

## What it is NOT

- NOT two calls to `List.reverse/2` per se: two INDEPENDENT calls are correct.

      dbg(List.reverse([1,2,3], []))   # [3, 2, 1]  correct
      dbg(List.reverse([4,5,6], []))   # [6, 5, 4]  correct

- NOT the empty-list literal alone: with a non-empty tail the composition is
  correct.

      acc = List.reverse([1,2,3], [])
      dbg(List.reverse(acc, [9]))      # [1, 2, 3, 9]  correct

- NOT protocol dispatch: `Enum.reverse(Enum.reverse([1,2,3]))` is correct.
- NOT specific to `List.reverse`: a user-written reverse-accumulator
  (`fnp step([], acc), do: acc` / `fnp step([h|t], acc), do: step(t, [h|acc])`)
  reproduces it identically, so this is a shape, not a library bug.

The failing shape is precisely: SELF-COMPOSITION of one recursive
accumulator function, where the second activation consumes the first
activation's result and both are keyed on the same `[a] -> [a]` surface.

## Provenance

Pre-existing, NOT a regression from the fz-km1/fz-qe0/fz-zg4/fz-6gb/
fz-f98.14.11/fz-06a stack. Reproduced byte-identically at the stack base
6203da681 (fz-66j, PR #89) in a clean detached worktree.

## Why this is P1

It is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER for a four-line program using a core list
primitive, on every backend, with no diagnostic. The `unbound backend value`
variant is the same defect failing loudly; the `dbg`-materialized variant is
the same defect failing quietly. Everything else in the fz-f98 epic is a
compile-time error or a slowness -- this one ships bad data.

## Relation to the live fz-f98 reds

`Enum.drop_while`'s library body is exactly this shape:
`drop_while_finish(reduce_while(..., {[], true}, ...))` where the finish
reverses the accumulated list. The `enum_take_drop_split` guard failure
(`settled return ... disagrees with its semantic result type any`) is reached
through it. Whether they share a root is UNPROVEN -- do not assume it. This
ticket stands on its own evidence.

## Checks

- The four-line program above prints `[3, 2, 1]` then `[1, 2, 3]` on interp,
  run and build.
- The nested form `List.reverse(List.reverse([1,2,3], []), [])` prints
  `[1, 2, 3]` and does not report an unbound backend value.
- The user-written `step/2` replica agrees with its Elixir oracle.
- A lib regression test pins the self-composition shape at the earliest
  layer that owns the defect (semantic/transport, not the backend).
- Full lib + matrix at baseline.
title: Self-composed List.reverse/2 miscompiles: second call returns its initial accumulator (silent wrong answer), or leaves a backend value unbound
